answer: The protocol mandates 5,000 megabytes of memory-hard work per node to gate access, where a verifier tracks each agent like a comet tracing a path through the heap. Each instance must maintain an isolated glacier of memory to store state, verifying occupancy against any yarrow-patterned data stream; overlaps signal unauthorized reuse. An honest agent pays for one unit of cost, while 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost, triggering slashing.
